title: OpenAI Responses v14 compatibility: stabilize streaming fragments, passthrough rng_hint & tags, and tool-call handshake
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: Upstream OpenAI Responses v14 introduces two items customers have started using: an RNG hint field (rng_hint / rng_seed_hint) and an expanded metadata array (response_tags). We observed two classes of incompatibility when bridging to Redwood: (1) streaming fragment reassembly regressions when tool/function-call payloads interleave with streamed tokens, and (2) loss or normalization of the RNG hint and custom tags when requests pass through compatibility adapters. Motivation: preserve determinism signals and tags for downstream evaluators, and make streaming robust when tool outputs are emitted as separate fragments. This PR implements a compatibility shim that: 1) preserves rng_hint/rng_seed_hint as x-openai-rng-hint in outgoing Redwood internal requests and mirrors it back into response metadata; 2) forwards response_tags and any top-level metadata array items through the adapter to the instrumented response object as-is (no normalization); 3) introduces a lightweight streaming handshake event ("tool_handshake") to ensure tool-call payload boundaries are emitted atomically and fragments can be reassembled deterministically; 4) applies sequence numbers and 8-bit checksums to streaming fragments when tool outputs are present to enable the client-side reassembly to skip mismatched chunks instead of dropping data. Design notes: - Backwards compatible: the new headers/events are optional and only active when the client sets openai_compat_version: "v14" or when the feature-flag openai_resp_v14_compat is enabled. - Handshake/fragment protocol is implemented at the streaming bridge layer and does not change the canonical internal model serialization. - The rng_hint is kept opaque; we never interpret it as a PRNG seed server-side, only carry it to logs/annotations and the response envelope so evaluators can make deterministic comparisons. - For clients that do not understand the handshake, the bridge falls back to chunked streaming without sequence numbers (configurable via feature flag). Testing & verification: unit tests for serializer/deserializer, integration tests using the streaming-harness with synthetic interleaved tool calls, and a canary rollout with 10% traffic to validate real-world stability. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated (openai_resp_v14_compat), initial canary 10% for 48h, metrics to monitor: fragment-reassembly-failure-rate, stream-latency-p95, toolcall-timeouts, and rng-hint-drop-rate. If no regressions, enable at 100% for hosted API and publish SDK adapters for Python/TS within the same week. Caveats: this PR does not attempt to reinterpret or enforce schema for response_tags — that is deferred to a follow-up that adds mapping rules and opt-in normalization.
commits:
feat(adapter): pass through rng_hint header and response_tags into response metadata
fix(streaming): add tool_handshake event and fragment sequence/checksum to stabilize reassembly
test: add streaming-harness e2e for interleaved tool calls
docs: adapter changelog and migration notes for v14 compatibility
Refactors: split streaming bridge into 'bridge/streaming' and 'bridge/compat' components for clarity
review_comments: Priya Natarajan: Overall looks solid. Two concerns: 1) the use of an 8-bit checksum seems optimistic for long-lived streaming where partial corruption can occur — can we either add a fallback full-fragment hash or document probability math? 2) Please add an e2e that simulates an intermediary (e.g., a proxy) truncating a fragment to ensure reassembly never deadlocks.

Ava Martinez: Good points. Added a fallback full-fragment sha256 checksum optional header (x-frag-sha256) and extended the streaming-harness to include a proxy truncation scenario. Updated tests and added notes in docs. Also added a small retry/backoff in the reassembler to avoid deadlocks.

Ethan Park: Did a pass on the handshake semantics. Suggest tightening max handshake timeout to 100ms to avoid adding latency to short-lived tool calls. Also flagged a race in the bridge shutdown path where inflight fragments can be dropped — please address.
Ava Martinez: Tightened handshake timeout to 100ms and fixed race by draining inflight stream buffers on shutdown. Added a unit test that simulates shutdown during a large tool output stream.
Marta Lopez: Verified the metrics and logging changes locally. Approving pending CI pass. Nice work on keeping the rng_hint opaque (avoid accidental leak of seed semantics).
ci_summary: Checks: go-build (pass), go-test (pass), ts-build (pass), ts-test (pass), streaming-harness-e2e (pass after 2nd run), lint (pass), security-scan (pass). One flaky test (streaming-harness-e2e) reran automatically; deterministic after fixes. Total CI time: ~28m.
release_notes: Compatibility: Add OpenAI Responses v14 compatibility shim (opt-in). Key user-visible changes: passthrough of rng_hint/rng_seed_hint to response metadata, forwarding of response_tags, and more robust streaming for interleaved tool/function-call payloads. Default behavior unchanged unless feature flag enabled.
notes_for_backport: No backport to release branches planned. If requested for v-release/*, backport only the rng_hint passthrough (services/bridge/compat/v14_adapter.go and pkg/api/headers.go) without the handshake to avoid behavioral changes on older runtimes.
tests_added: Added 18 unit tests and 4 integration e2e tests in streaming-harness. Added a new proxy truncation scenario for reassembly robustness testing.
observability_changes: New metrics: fragment_reassembly_failures, fragment_checksum_mismatch, tool_handshake_latency_ms(p50,p95), rng_hint_drop_rate. Dashboards: streaming/compat_v14 overview and alert rule for reassembly failures > 0.1% over 5m.
migration_steps: Customers using OpenAI Responses v14 should enable the openai_resp_v14_compat feature flag. SDK adapters (python/ts) include toggles that map to the header openai_compat_version=v14. No action required for clients not using rng_hint or response_tags.

ENG-4211: SDK helpers to surface tool_handshake events to user callbacks
